i18n.hindiRisk: SEVERE. Only 6 stringResource calls exist in the whole file (R.string.home_open_job :424, home_retry :654/:923/:1262, home_continue_job :774, settings_language_title/subtitle :982-983, settings_delete_account_* :1027-1028, home_availability_online/offline :157-160) against 35+ hardcoded English literals. values-hi/strings.xml has full parity for the keys that exist (163 strings in both values/ and values-hi/), so the Hindi build will render a bilingual mongrel: Hindi buttons inside English cards. Layout-wise the five bottom-tab labels are single English words in `maxLines = 1` (:247) — Hindi equivalents ("उपलब्धता", "कमाई") are longer and will ellipsize. StatTile is height-locked at 94.dp with maxLines=1 labels (:493, :514, :520) so longer Devanagari will truncate rather than wrap. SettingCard subtitles are capped at maxLines = 2 (:1133).
i18n.currencyFormatting: formatRupees(paise) = "Rs %,.0f".format(paise / 100.0) — TechnicianHomeScreen.kt:1350. Uses ASCII 'Rs ' not the ₹ glyph; %,.0f applies the default JVM locale grouping, which under an English/Hindi (India) locale gives Western thousands grouping in most JVM configurations rather than the Indian lakh/crore pattern (1,00,000) that Ayodhya technicians read — [inferred, depends on runtime locale provider]. Paise are rounded away, so ₹499.50 shows as 'Rs 500'. Rendered at :465, :557, :563, :609, :752.

35+ user-facing strings are hardcoded English in an app whose target users are Hindi-speaking technicians in rural UP; values-hi/strings.xml exists with full 163-key parity but this screen bypasses it almost entirely

loading.quality: There is no loading state. During the accept network call the primary button merely swaps its label to 'Accepting…' and disables (JobOfferScreen.kt:236-243) — no spinner, no progress. On a rural 2G connection the technician sees a dead button for seconds with no indication anything is happening.

empty.quality: Idle renders 'Offer unavailable' in a centred card. It is a dead end — no dismiss button, no way back; the screen only disappears when the ViewModel state changes (AppNavigation.kt:176).

i18n.hindiRisk: HIGH. Copy is properly externalized (12 job_offer_* keys, all present in values-hi/strings.xml) but the LAYOUT cannot absorb Hindi. The Offering column is fillMaxSize with Arrangement.SpaceBetween and no verticalScroll (JobOfferScreen.kt:142-149), so a longer Hindi service name (headlineSmall, no maxLines at :179-184) plus a multi-line Devanagari address in HsInfoRow will push the accept/decline buttons off-screen on a small handset with no way to scroll to them — the technician physically cannot accept the job. Note also that job_offer_accepting in values-hi is stored as numeric character references rather than literal Devanagari (values-hi/strings.xml:18) while its neighbours are literal text, an inconsistency worth verifying renders correctly.
i18n.currencyFormatting: HsPriceText(pricePaise = offer.amountPaise.toInt()) — JobOfferScreen.kt:216, which renders "Rs ${pricePaise / 100}" at design-system/src/main/kotlin/com/homeservices/designsystem/components/HsComponents.kt:172. ASCII 'Rs' not ₹, integer division silently truncates paise, and there is no digit grouping at all — so ₹12,500 displays as 'Rs 12500' with no lakh/crore or even thousands separator. The Long→Int cast at :216 is also a narrowing conversion.

The technician-app has only one photographic drawable available (res/drawable-nodpi/tech_field_ac_service.png) and this screen references none

animationsUsed.what: animateFloatAsState on the countdown ring progress, label 'countdown', default spring — not a HomeservicesMotion duration/easing
Haptic EFFECT_TICK vibration in the final 5 seconds, fired from LaunchedEffect(uiState); because the key is the whole uiState it re-fires on every one-second tick from 5 down to 1

motion.transitionsOnNav: None. The screen is drawn as a bare conditional child of the root Box (AppNavigation.kt:176-181) with no AnimatedVisibility, so a full-screen, high-stakes interrupt materialises and vanishes as an instant hard cut. The Offering→Accepted/Declined/Expired transitions inside the screen (:85-116) are equally uncrossfaded — the whole layout snaps to a single centred card.

surfaces.density: Top-heavy and hollow. Arrangement.SpaceBetween over fillMaxSize with only three children (:147) means whatever vertical slack exists is dumped as two large voids — between the countdown and the detail card, and between the card and the buttons. On a tall device the screen reads as three islands floating in dead space; on a short device the same layout overflows with no scroll. Padding values are 16 / 18 / 14 / 10 / 24.dp — five different rhythms in 282 lines.

observations.claim: The Offering layout is a non-scrolling fillMaxSize Column, so on a small screen or with longer Hindi/Devanagari content the Accept and Decline buttons are pushed out of the viewport and the offer becomes impossible to act on
The countdown ring divides by a hardcoded 30f rather than the offer's actual TTL, so if dispatch issues any window other than 30 seconds the ring is desynchronised from the number inside it
Accept and Decline are both full-width, both stacked, and separated by only 10.dp — the accept action is not unmistakable, and a mis-tap on a bouncing scroll-free layout permanently forfeits the job
Decline fires immediately with no confirmation — a single tap irreversibly rejects the offer and clears it from the bus
Error copy exposes a raw HTTP status code to a rural technician and is hardcoded English inside the ViewModel, so it can never be translated

The urgency signal is binary — the ring stays calm primary green for 25 of 30 seconds then abruptly turns red, with no progressive escalation of colour, scale or motion
Money renders as 'Rs 12500' — ASCII Rs, paise truncated by integer division, and no digit grouping whatsoever, on the screen where the technician decides whether the job is worth taking
The haptic is keyed on the whole uiState inside LaunchedEffect, so it re-triggers on each one-second recomposition from 5 to 1 — five separate ticks rather than a designed escalation pattern

placeholderOrMissing: No map, no route line, no ETA and no navigate affordance despite the app having full maps plumbing — StartTripUseCase.kt:20 emits NavigationEvent.Maps and HomeGraph.kt:181 launches the maps intent, but that fires only as a side effect of the Start-trip transition; there is no visible 'Navigate' button the technician can tap again later

The PhotoCaptureScreen overlay (:102) and CompletionConfirmationDialog (:116) both appear with no enter transition beyond M3 dialog defaults.

The failure is horizontal — StatusStepper spreads five fixed 58.dp columns with Arrangement.SpaceBetween across the full width (:217-221), so on a wide device the dots drift far apart with nothing connecting them, and the 16.dp dots leave the row looking sparse and unfinished.

observations.claim: The Error state is dead code — ActiveJobUiState.Error is rendered here but never constructed anywhere in the app, so a booking that fails to load leaves the technician staring at a skeleton indefinitely with no error and no way out

The safety escalation feature is built but never shown: ActiveJobViewModel sets showShieldSheet = true (ActiveJobViewModel.kt:338) and ShieldReportSheet.kt:30 exists, but ActiveJobScreen never renders it and no other file references it — a technician in danger has no reachable panic affordance
The mock-GPS warning is computed and stored in state (ActiveJobViewModel.kt:321, :330) but the screen never renders mockLocationWarning, so a spoofed-location detection is silently swallowed
There is no way to contact the customer — no name, no phone, no call or message button anywhere on the live job screen
There is no visible Navigate/maps affordance; the maps intent only auto-fires once as a side effect of the Start-trip transition, so a technician who dismisses it cannot re-open directions
Tapping the primary CTA gives no in-flight feedback — no spinner, no disabled state, no optimistic stage advance — so on a slow connection the technician taps repeatedly

The stepper's incomplete steps use surfaceVariant dots on surface (~1.2:1) with onSurfaceVariant captions, so four of the five stages are visually near-invisible and the component fails to communicate progress
Stepper columns are hard-locked to 58.dp with unbounded labelSmall captions and no overflow handling — Hindi stage labels will wrap or clip

loading.quality: Upload progress is a bare 20.dp CircularProgressIndicator swapped in place of the 'Confirm & Upload' label — the button silently changes width as the label disappears, and there is no percentage, no byte count and no cancel. There is NO loading state for camera initialisation: between mount and ProcessCameraProvider resolving (:133-155) the technician sees a pure black screen with a prompt floating on it and no indication the camera is starting.

empty.quality: Not applicable to a camera surface.

error.quality: PARTIAL AND LEAKY. The upload-failure overlay interpolates the raw exception message into R.string.photo_upload_failed ('Upload failed: %s', values/strings.xml:101) — the source value is exceptionOrNull()?.message from ActiveJobViewModel.kt:255, so a technician can be shown a Java exception string. Worse, the CAPTURE failure path is completely silent: ImageCapture.OnImageSavedCallback.onError has an empty body with a comment (:193), so a shutter that fails leaves capturedPath null and the button appears simply not to work.

success.quality: MAJOR: there is no success confirmation. On a successful upload the overlay simply disappears (driven by the parent clearing pendingPhotoStage) — no checkmark, no 'photo saved', no haptic. The technician gets no positive proof that the evidence photo, which gates their payment, was actually stored.

offline.quality: No connectivity check before or during upload. An offline technician taps Confirm & Upload, waits on a spinner, and eventually receives a raw exception string. The queue-and-retry machinery exists (PhotoUploadRetryBanner.kt:33) but this overlay never tells the user that queueing is an option.

permissionDenied.quality: Present but minimal: 'Camera permission required' (values/strings.xml:106) with no explanation of WHY the photo is needed, no illustration, and — critically — no handling of permanent denial. Once the user selects 'Don't allow' twice, permissionLauncher.launch (:110) is a no-op on Android 11+, so the Grant-permission button becomes a dead button with no route to app settings. The camera branches use full-bleed scrims with 16.dp padding (:171, :210, :233, :276) which is fine, but the fallback branches (permission denied :319, no camera :119, upload error :254) all use 24.dp padding with 12.dp spacing on unanchored centred columns, so the error and permission states float as loose text in a black void with no card, no surface and no visual containment. The 48.dp magic bottom offset on the shutter (:201) sits it awkwardly above the nav-bar padding while the Cancel button beside it uses only 16.dp (:210), so the two bottom controls are on different baselines.
